[C2 decision by pep-c2-reconciler-java-co-r1 (independent non-author reconciler, Claude Opus 5.5 subagent) on 2026-11-26 for author pep-c2-author-java-classes-and-objects (Claude Opus 5.5, artifact author), reviewing artifact.html 2b46ec09f6c23324e3f7bd0ff1829fea45764065263b16eff3ae3b76733b75e7] accept. Shared engine defect S1 (pep-classes-objects-engine v3, byte-identical on all nine pages): member() reads method and constructor bodies with balanced("{","}") only, so a body statement without its ";" (or with unbalanced parentheses) is never reported. Reproduced by this reconciler headless on both roots: on main (dd228138, engine v2) and on this branch, e.g. classes-and-objects "return pages > 300" without ";" gets 6 of 6 and the done text, and enums label() ending "}" instead of "};" gets 8 of 8. The gap is pre-existing, but v3 makes it worse: a check that fails only because a ";" is missing now headlines "Almost" (constructors: "Almost: 4 of 5 checks pass. event is not set from its parameter yet" on main read "Not yet"). Fix now in this correction loop. Add one bounded statement pass to the shared reader, run before any check: split each body at depth 0, require every simple statement (declaration, assignment, call, return, throw, this(...), including one whose expression holds braces such as a switch expression) to end with ";", accept a control statement (if/else, for, while, do, switch statement) whose body is either a block or a single statement ending in ";" (an unbraced body such as "if (x) throw ...;" is legal Java and must stay accepted), require balanced () and [] inside each statement, report only what javac certainly rejects, leave any shape the pass cannot classify to the checks exactly as today, and report a missing ";" as error: ';' expected at the end of the line that lacks it (after() of the last token, not the next line). This uses the existing reader-error path ("This does not count as a try"). Its two effects, stated so the captain can overrule them: code with a body syntax error stops earning credit, and such an attempt stops consuming a try (it becomes a reader error, as a field-level missing ";" already is on main and here); the attempt and credit rules themselves do not change. Reword the scope line, data-static-alt and the no-JS "What the practice editor reads" paragraph (which today claims it "checks declarations and statement shapes, and reports anything else as not supported") so they state what is checked: declarations, statement endings and brackets, not names, types or reachability. Checking names, types, unreachable statements or constructor cycles is out of scope for this loop (deferred to a checker-hardening pass). Scope judgment used throughout this reconciliation: making the reader or a check reject code that javac rejects, or accept code that javac accepts, is check correctness; it leaves the attempt and credit rules untouched (reader errors and not-supported limits already "do not count as a try" in the v2 and v3 engine, and credit rules are unchanged). If the captain rules that this counts as a grading change, every high that depends on it must be re-decided as escalate. Shared engine defect S2: a field initializer without its ";" lets expr() run on through the next member, so the error lands on a later line. v3 made this actively misleading: it added after() and the plain() sentence "Add a semicolon (;) at the end of line N" for that wrong N. Reproduced by this reconciler: classes-and-objects "int pages = 0" (no ";") reports line 8 on main and "Add a semicolon (;) at the end of line 7" on this branch, while the missing ";" is on line 3; constructors "int seat = 0" reports line 13 on main and line 12 here. Fix now in this correction loop. In the field-initializer expr(), stop at a depth-0 token on a later line that starts a new member (a modifier, or a type followed by an identifier and "(" or "="), and report error: ';' expected at after() of the initializer's last token, so the line shown is the field's own line (practice-feedback-policy 1.3). Reader-error path, not a try. Page note: all four cases reproduced by this reconciler on this branch: (1) "private int current = 18" without ";" gives "Almost: 5 of 6 checks pass. Keep the field offset." and spends a try (main gave "Not yet" with the same false reason); (2) line 4 is reported as line 16; (4) the ";" after "return current" or "t.setTarget(21)" is ignored. S1 and S2 fix these. (3) "pubic int reading()" gets the v3 plain() sentence "Add a semicolon (;) at the end of line 10": the semicolon advice is added to any ";"-expected error, which is wrong for a misspelt word. Fix now as well: when an unknown word stands before a type at the start of a member, report that it is not a Java keyword and to check its spelling on that line (reader-error path, not a try). A recheck must observe all four cases reported as problems on the line to change, none of them as a check failure, an "Almost" or a pass.
